glamsterdam_eip8037_impact.highlight: EIP-8037 and EIP-8038 break smart contract invariants; central topic of call
EIPs enable 3.3x gas scaling (60M → 200M gas/block) but break hard-coded gas patterns
Delays in audits and outreach caused by EF reorgs and budget cuts; Marius accepts responsibility
Combined search: 200 total findings (152 ChainSecurity + EF internal); coverage not complete
Majority of findings from Invariants 4 and 7: hard-coded gas budgets insufficient post-Glamsterdam

audit_findings.highlight: ChainSecurity: 152 findings across mainnet; reservoir/refill mechanism is minority of breakage
Dedaub: 12 high + 70 medium confirmed findings from ~25K contracts with non-trivial gas patterns
EF internal: 3 highs (1 fixed, 2 fixing within a month); at least 25 confirmed mediums; 16 actively triaging
OP Stack chains independently affected; OP has fixed invariants, live on OP Sepolia

app_developer_concerns.highlight: Jango (Juicebox): EIP-8037 allows users to tune gas and trigger catch blocks, breaking composability
Daniel (Uniswap): reservoir mechanism introduces implicit user-controlled branching; fundamentally breaks try-catch
Neville (Dedaub): no reliable way for callers to distinguish OOG revert from logical revert
Barnabas: Ethereum cannot honestly promise true immutability given known upcoming PQ/state changes

protocol_rationale_and_tradeoffs.highlight: ~10–15K contracts affected out of ~90M on Ethereum; immutable broken contracts hold ~$300–500K
No silver bullet: any 2D gas version breaks something; removing 8037 also blocks large contract deployment
Affected protocols signaling willingness to fix indicate a January Glamsterdam date is acceptable
Glamsterdam is a precondition for Hegota (PQ); removing it delays post-quantum accounts by ~4 months

process_improvements.highlight: Toni: core devs must clearly define which invariants are guaranteed vs. likely to change
Marius: proposal to publish EIP documenting stable vs. expected-to-change protocol invariants
Specs team (Mario/danceratopz): two open PRs adding deployed-idiom invariant corpus and chain invariant checks
EF/Ethlabs agent-swarm analysis was largely automatable; will be run systematically for future EIPs
EF Access Layer (Rahul): builder enablement team surveyed 50+ teams; direct contacts for 3,000+ L1 devs

eip_process.highlight: jochem-brouwer: large influx of AI-generated EIPs; EIPIP call Wednesday Nov 18 16:00 UTC to discuss AI integration into review process

action_items.action: Review and merge specs PRs #3948 and #3982 (deployed-idiom invariant corpus and chain invariant checks)
Decide on Glamsterdam path forward (ship 8037 as-is vs. changes) and agree on Hoodi date
Coordinate outreach to remaining affected L2/app teams not yet triaging; use direct security contacts

decisions.decision: No decision on EIP-8037 today; formal path-forward decision deferred to ACDE on Thursday
Glamsterdam delay was justified to prioritize app-layer mitigation time before mainnet

targets.target: Glamsterdam mainnet targeting January 2026 (per protocol signals from affected teams)
EIPIP call: Wednesday November 18, 16:00 UTC — AI integration into EIP review process
